lead: Power-calibrated invariance framework for event-log failure prediction (the 'Predictive Invariance Profile').
one_line: A power-calibrated assay determines which structural channel (presence / multiplicity / order / token-timing) is genuinely predictive; on real traces the signal is approximately invariant to within-window order AND token-specific timing.

order_assay.power: 10% injected order detected at order_value 0.082 (monotone to 0.271)

timing_assay.power: 10% injected token-timing detected at recency_value 0.079 (monotone to 0.293)
timing_assay.real_traces: null: sepsis +0.024 (<0.03 bar), Kelmarsh/Alibaba ~0; synthetic Azure +0.058

validated_components.presence: dominant channel across all useful-signal traces

two_symmetric_confounds.apparent_order_is_multiplicity: Alibaba naive sequence gain collapses under the count-preserving null (already in paper).
two_symmetric_confounds.apparent_timing_is_generic_proximity: Naive recency gain reflects [window span, time-since-last-event] (AUROC 0.73-0.97 even at fixed count); token-specific timing near-null once generic proximity is preserved in the null.

proposed_confirmatory_experiment: Calibrated 4-channel recovery benchmark: presence-only / multiplicity-only / order-only / timing-only injections, each modifying ONLY its channel; show the assay recovers each (diagonal channel x detection matrix).
proposed_figure: Ground-truth channel x detected-channel matrix (rows: 5 real traces + 4 injections; cols: presence/multiplicity/order/timing value) + injection recovery curves.
proposed_title: What Information Predicts Failure? Power-Calibrated Invariance Tests for Event Logs
